newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - RTZ says De Beers role in Canada site unclear.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - RTZ says De Beers role in Canada site unclear.

text.p: The chief executive of global mining house RTZ Corp-CRA Ltd, Robert Wilson, said it was too early to say if De Beers Consolidated Mines would have a role in the marketing of diamonds from the Diavik project in Canada's North West Territories.

Wilson, speaking from London to mining analysts and funds managers, said the exclusion of De Beers' Central Selling Organisation from the marketing of Argyle diamonds earlier this year did not mean the same situation would occur in Canada.
"The answer is it (Australia's Argyle decision) doesn't imply anything one way or the other," he said.
"We are still several years away fom commencing production at the North West Territories. We are a long way yet from determining the marketing of the product," he said.
"They are in our minds two quite distinct commercial decisions."

Wilson said development of the Canadian project, in which RTZ-CRA has 60 percent with the remainder held by Aber Resources Ltd, could begin with production from the smaller A-418 kimberlite pipe which has an indicated grade of 4.02 carats per tonne. The larger A-154 South pipe, 700 metres away, has a sample grade of 4.6 carats/tonne.
"The results (from A-154 South) support earlier indications of an inferred resource of 8.4 million tonnes down to 250 metres," the company said in briefing notes for analysts.
"Initial valuation suggests approximately US$260 per tonne of kimberlite and compares favourably with operating mines around the world."

Australia's Argyle joint venture said in June it would sell its huge but low quality diamond output directly, ending talks with the CSO and competing with the world's largest distributor. RTZ-CRA has 56.8 percent of the Argyle partnership.
